newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end stronger, energy sector gains.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end stronger, energy sector gains.

text.p: * New Zealand shares end strongly
* TrustPower, BOP Electricity, FCL Energy post sharp gains
* Sky City recovers ground. Ceramco eases, post-result
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
318 +1 * NZSC cap index +18.69 at 4,850.49
365 -5 * Volume NZ$66 million. Futures +3 at 1,178
755 +5 * Other movers - +34 +30
New Zealand shares ended Wednesday's trade on a stronger note, led by Telecom and a strong performance in energy stocks.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 9.51 points higher at 2,351.84 on turnover worth NZ$66 million.
TrustPower, up 34 cents at $2.60, and Bay of Plenty Electricity, up 30 at $7.10, were the among the strongest performers in the energy sector.

Richard Burton and Cavill White Securities said there was a rumour circulating that something may be happening between TrustPower, Bay of Plenty and Power New Zealand, which bought into BOP at just over NZ$8.00 a share mid-year.
A Power NZ spokesman said he was unaware of any such moves between the three.
Utilities investor Infratil, which has a stake in TrustPower, was up 10 cents at NZ$1.23.
Fletcher Energy, which sold its BOP holding mid-year, was up seven cents at NZ$4.19 but the rise was more likely to be a reflection of stronger oil prices, Burton said.
Telecom gained five to NZ$7.55, following strength on Wall Street overnight.
Casino operator Sky City regained ground after a sharp sell-down on Tuesday, ending 10 cents higher at NZ$8.15.
Troubled apparel and ceramics group Ceramco lost one cent to NZ$1.16 after posting a first half loss of NZ$1.63 million.
Ceramco said the short term outlook for apparel was uncertain, but that it expected a return to profitability in the June 1998 year.
